title: Recall & fidelity checker for cost-driven cache changes
creator: Marcus Chen
description: Objective: build an evaluation harness that detects quality regressions specifically caused by batching and KV-cache configuration changes aimed at reducing token/unit cost. Focus on recall and fidelity (not just token-level perplexity) across production-like prompts. Deliverables: 1) golden prompt corpus tailored to batch/cache edge cases, 2) a lightweight statistical test runner for canary & canary-to-production comparisons, 3) automated rollback triggers and human-in-the-loop review flows, 4) dashboards with per-route quality vs cost delta visualization. Rationale: existing regressions frequently manifest as missing entities, dropped context, or hallucinated completions after aggressive cache/batch heuristics. Traditional token-loss metrics miss these. This ticket scopes the checker with pragmatic acceptance thresholds and an implementation plan suitable for runtime rollout and Dedicated autoscale experiments.
acceptance_criteria: Golden corpus assembled with >= 600 unique prompts spanning short/long contexts, multi-turn chat, and prompt-engineered edge cases
Automated run produces recall/fidelity score per route and overall change metric
Quality delta thresholds: recall drop <= 1.0% and semantic-fidelity metric change <= 0.015 (defined in spec) for progressive apply
Statistical test: paired bootstrap or permutation test with p < 0.05 on a 1k-sample baseline or equivalent power
Canary policy: block rollforward when any high-severity route shows >2% recall regression or customer-impact flagged examples
Human review workflow integrates with Slack alert + Redwood Console review link for blocked applies
comments: 2025-02-21 — Marcus Chen: Initial spike completed. Benchmarked several fidelity metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding cosine + a light entailment model). Found embedding cosine more correlated with human judgments on our internal sample than perplexity for cache regressions.

2025-02-24 — Asha Patel: Drafted golden prompt selection criteria (diversity by length, named-entity heavy, multi-turn reference, structured JSON outputs). Will curate from recent prod logs and synthesize hard negatives.

2025-02-27 — Priya Desai (PM): Reviewed thresholds. Suggest tightening recall threshold for high-value routes (payments, legal) and allow looser thresholds for low-impact ones. Added per-route override table to scope.
2025-03-01 — Design review (Lena Rodriguez): UX for Console review modal looks good; added request to surface example diff snippets and anchor to original input with tokens highlighted.

2025-03-04 — Marcus Chen: Prototype runner added to repo: uses paired-permutation test, supports sample sharding, and emits JSON summary artifact compatible with Console ingestion. Ran against dedicated autoscale trace and found a 1.4% recall drop on one internal route with aggressive cache TTL=120s; flagged for follow-up.
2025-03-05 — Asha Patel: Decided on canary window of 48 hours and minimum sample size of 600 per route. Next: wire automated apply/rollback hooks and create an alert runbook for on-call.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: stricter thresholds reduce rollout velocity but prevent silent customer regressions; will pilot per-customer relaxations for internal perf experiments.
We will reuse parts of the existing eval harness but add route-aware weighting and entity-level recall checks.
Follow-up tickets: integrate an entailment model to capture semantic deletions (ENG-11890), expand golden corpus with multi-lingual examples (ENG-12012).
